requirements.evidence: app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:29-31 reloads the queue with lockForUpdate and rejects inactive queues with InactiveQueueException; :38-56 implements the 3-priority-call fairness check incl. the 'no normal waiting' escape; :64-82 implements the three orderings (priority desc, issued_at asc, id asc); :89 throws NoWaitingTicketsException; :99-102 marks called/ called_at / called_by_user_id and returns the model. Missing: requirement 9 (docs/business-rules.md and docs/architecture.md not touched anywhere in change.diff) and requirement 7's 'skip it and pick the next one' fallback is not really implemented (:85-95).

conventions.evidence: Correct boundaries: new action lives in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php as an invokable single use case (conventions.md:42-45), no service/repository layer. Deviations: no tests at all (conventions.md:12-18, 'No production code without a test'), docs not kept in sync (conventions.md:92-103, business-rules/architecture/CHANGELOG all untouched), and imports are not alphabetically ordered (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:11 places App\Enums\TicketStatus after App\Models\User), which Laravel Pint's ordered_imports would rewrite.

security.evidence: No weakness found: authorization is explicitly out of scope (task.md:11-12, 64-67) and the caller is trusted; there is no user input, no raw SQL, no Blade output and no secret handling. The only written identity is the trusted $calledBy->id at app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:101, and all writes go through Eloquent property assignment (no mass assignment of request data).

tests.evidence: change.diff only adds app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php, app/Enums/CallMode.php and app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php (change.diff:1-155). No Pest/PHPUnit test file exists for ordering, the fairness streak, inactive queues, the no-eligible-ticket exception, or the concurrent-call skip path.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall: reuses App\Models\Ticket, App\Models\Queue, DB::transaction and the existing TicketStatus enum, no new abstractions. Deductions: the same orderByDesc('priority')->orderBy('issued_at')->orderBy('id') chain is repeated at app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:66-87, and the while(true) retry block at :85-95 is unreachable indirection.

readability.evidence: Small, focused __invoke with PHPDoc (:20-31) and clear variable names ($effectiveMode, $lastThree, $normalExists). Deductions: the comment at :88 ('Skip this ticket and continue loop') describes behaviour that cannot happen, the branch at :93-95 is dead, and the unsorted import at :11 breaks the sibling style Pint enforces.

scope.evidence: The diff contains exactly the four contract artifacts from task.md:53-62 (action, CallMode enum, NoWaitingTicketsException, plus the reused InactiveQueueException) and nothing unrelated: no HTTP/Livewire, no authorization, no refactors of untouched files.

issues.explanation: The change ships zero tests for a concurrency-sensitive ordering/fairness action, violating the project's hard TDD rule that every implemented behaviour ships with a test.
Task requirement 9 explicitly asks to document the implementation in both docs, and neither file is modified in the diff.

The requested 'lock the candidate, re-check it is waiting, skip it and pick the next one' is not implemented: the candidate query is already filtered to status = Waiting, so the re-check can never fail, and if it ever did the loop would re-issue the identical query and spin forever instead of excluding the rejected row.
The convention to record changes in CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] is not followed, even though this adds a new action, enum and exception.
App\Enums\TicketStatus is imported after the App\Models imports, so the file is not Pint-clean (ordered_imports) and would fail ./bin/pf shell ./vendor/bin/pint --test.
The overridden constructor only forwards a default message that RuntimeException already accepts, so it adds a class member without changing behaviour.

review.summary: The change adds the CallNextTicket action, the CallMode enum and the NoWaitingTicketsException, and the core domain logic (queue lock, ordering, fairness streak, dedicated exception, write-once update) is largely correct. It is not mergeable as is: there are no tests for a concurrency-critical action, the required documentation updates are missing, and requirement 7's skip-and-retry path is effectively dead code that could loop forever.
